description: Build 32 pragmatic feature slots from quote-selected utterances, normalized UD observations, cues and paragraph metadata; source-qualified previous-act indices and training dictionaries.
state: 32 slots; quote intervals are UTF-8 bounds when produced by quote_spans; dictionary order is training traversal order; source isolation is distinct from licensing. This feature module does not enforce train/evaluation separation.
cost: With B text bytes, W words, P cues, maximum phrase L, row costs O(B+W*P*L) plus annotation; annotation cost is external. Quote state scans allocate O(B); predecessor map expected O(N) time/space; dictionaries expected O(total string bytes) hashing and storage.
forward: For item i, extract resets quote state unless adjacent input has equal source/doc/paragraph and ordinal +1, excluding Tatoeba. quote_spans feeds row; row invokes the real annotator through row_with, producing 32 slots in SLOTS order with prev=start. prev_of independently builds source/doc/ordinal predecessors. Dict builds per-slot first-observation IDs with previous-act vocabulary seeded before rows.
inverse: Universe: valid item sequences, supplied annotation observations, valid cue tables and dictionaries paired with candidate rows/indices/IDs. Absent behavior includes a row with a different slot count, prev initialized to an act, a Tatoeba predecessor, a predecessor from another source, or an encoded missing value other than UNSEEN. These are source-derived constraints (inner bound), not an exhaustive complement of live annotation.

Compatible antecedents retain every item text, quote state, annotation and cue configuration satisfying all observed coordinates and IDs. Normalization, buckets, omitted punctuation and discarded dictionary index prevent unique recovery. Equal rows may arise from distinct casing, text and annotations; IDs additionally require the exact dictionary.
limitations: Supplied Word fixtures only; no live annotation/model loading, corpus, teacher, GPU or held-out measurements.
Partial syntax, source-derived models and finite checks do not establish general correctness or approximation bounds.
Malformed dictionary widths/indices and arbitrary span inputs remain outside the validated domain.
